arrival.speaker: Narrator
arrival.dialogue:
Rain has stopped, but the street hasn't agreed to it yet. Water runs down the gutter in long brown ribbons, carrying cigarette filters toward a drain that gave up years ago.

Above a steel door: a neon sign. **N O X**. The *O* is dead. It has been dead for a long time, and nobody inside has ever thought about it.

The bass comes up through the pavement rather than through the air. You feel it in your shins before your ears admit it exists.

the-door.speaker: Narrator
the-door.dialogue:
A man stands in front of the door the way a boulder stands in front of a cave — not guarding, exactly. *Being* the obstacle.

He is enormous in the shoulders and precise in the hands. Shaved scalp, wet with mist. A bomber jacket that has been mended, not replaced. A little strip of tape on his lapel with a name written in marker: **GLEM**.

glem-speaks.speaker: Glem
glem-speaks.dialogue:
(He does not look up. He is scraping something off his thumbnail.)
"Line's the line. Door's the door."

(A pause. He finally raises his eyes, and takes both of you in — one long, unhurried inventory, the way a man reads a weather report for a day he's already decided to work.)

"...Huh."

inland-check.speaker: Inland Empire
inland-check.dialogue:
*This door is not a door tonight. It is a mouth, and it has been chewing since ten o'clock.*

*Something in there wants to be found. Not by him. He's just the tooth. Something further in, past the red light, sitting very still and waiting for you specifically.*

*You will know it when the music changes.*

the-queue.speaker: Narrator
the-queue.dialogue:
Behind the velvet rope — which is not velvet, and is in fact a length of orange mooring line — eleven people are being patient in the cold.

A girl in a plastic raincoat reapplies lipstick using the reflection in a parked motor carriage. Two boys in matching corduroy pretend not to be brothers. Somebody near the back is quietly, methodically drunk.

Nobody talks to Glem. There is a two-metre radius around him that the queue respects like a religious rule.

glem-again.speaker: Glem
glem-again.dialogue:
(He shifts his weight. The pavement creaks. He tucks his hands into his armpits — cold, but unwilling to admit it in front of the line.)

"Whatever it is," he says to no one, to the wet street, to the dead *O* above his head, "you can do it out here or you can not do it. Those're the two."

taking-it-in.speaker: Narrator
taking-it-in.dialogue:
The mist is thickening again. Somewhere behind the steel door, the music drops into something slower, something with a heartbeat in it.

You are standing in the street outside NOX. Nothing has happened yet. Everything is still possible, in the exhausting way that everything always is.

options.label: (Look up at the dead letter in the sign.)
(Say nothing. Let the bass work on your shins.)

watch-glem-node.speaker: Narrator
watch-glem-node.dialogue:
His knuckles are scarred in the flat, dull way of a man who hits things that don't move much. But his boots are polished. *Polished.* In this weather.

He notices you noticing. He does not react. That, somehow, is the reaction.

watch-sign-node.speaker: Inland Empire
watch-sign-node.dialogue:
*N—X.* A gap where a letter should be. A held breath in the middle of a word.

*You could fall through a gap like that.*

arrival.speaker: Narrator
arrival.dialogue:
The street smells of three things at once: wet asphalt, frying oil from somewhere two buildings east, and the sour-sweet chemical breath of a club exhaling through a vent grate at ankle height.

Neon overhead. **N O X**, minus the *O*. The dead tube still ticks faintly as it tries to strike and fails.

the-door.speaker: Narrator
the-door.dialogue:
The doorway is a slab of grey steel with a repainted dent in it, roughly waist-height, roughly the shape of a shoulder.

In front of it stands the largest static object on this street that is technically a person. Shaved head, mended bomber jacket, tape on the lapel: **GLEM**, in marker, in his own handwriting.

perception-check.speaker: Perception (Sight)
perception-check.dialogue:
You take him apart without touching him.

  • Left ear: swollen, old. He has been grabbed by the head before, professionally.
  • Right jacket pocket: sags. Something short and dense. Not a gun — no grip shape. A roll of coins, maybe.
  • Boots: mirror-polished, and *dry*, when the street is not. He arrived by carriage, or he was let in the back at some point tonight.
  • His eyes track the queue in a slow left-to-right sweep every eleven seconds. Trained. Bored. Consistent.

*And: a second door. Painted the same grey, four metres to the right, half-hidden by a stack of crates. No handle on this side.*

glem-speaks.speaker: Glem
glem-speaks.dialogue:
"Line's the line. Door's the door."

(He says it flat, worn smooth by repetition — a phrase that stopped being sentences a thousand nights ago.)

(Then the eleven-second sweep reaches you, and stops early. He holds it. One beat too long.)
"...Huh."

the-queue.speaker: Narrator
the-queue.dialogue:
Eleven people wait behind an orange mooring rope pretending to be a velvet one. A girl in a plastic raincoat does her lipstick in a car window. Two boys in matching corduroy stand a deliberate metre apart.

Nobody stands within two metres of Glem. It's not written down anywhere. Everyone knows it.

glem-again.speaker: Glem
glem-again.dialogue:
(He rolls his neck. Something in it clicks audibly, twice.)

"Whatever it is," he tells the street, "you can do it out here, or you can not do it. Those're the two."

(The thing in his right pocket shifts when he moves. It chinks.)

taking-it-in.speaker: Narrator
taking-it-in.dialogue:
Behind the steel, the music drops into something slower. Through the ankle-height vent, the sound arrives with a faint delay, like the building is speaking twice.

You are outside NOX. Nothing has been decided. The rain is thinking about coming back.

options.label: (Listen to what's leaking out of the vent.)
(Keep an eye on that second grey door.)

listen-node.speaker: Perception (Hearing)
listen-node.dialogue:
Under the bass: a woman laughing in the register people use when they are not amused. Glass on glass. And once — briefly — a man's voice raised, then cut off very cleanly, as if a hand went over it.

*Somebody in there is already having a worse night than you.*

second-door-node.speaker: Narrator
second-door-node.dialogue:
The crates in front of it are stacked wrong — too neat, too far from the wall. Room enough for a person to stand behind them and not be seen from the queue.

The paint at the door's edge is chipped bright silver. Recently, and often, opened.
